I farm the same 4.1 mu in wheat-maize rotation, so I will run the whole piece through the year, not split it. I am old now, and the land is small, so I count every bag. But I still will not cut fertilizer too hard, because if the crop goes thin, that loss is bigger than wasting a little fertilizer. I do mostly what worked for me last year, then I look around the village and follow what the fields with good stands are doing.

For wheat, I will keep it steady. Wheat here drinks more water than maize, and since I have well irrigation, I will not let it sit dry at the key times. I will use improved seed, rotary the land after maize, put most of the phosphorus and potassium in first, and split the nitrogen so the wheat does not run out later. I will watch for weeds and disease and spray about two times if the field shows pressure. If the season is normal, I will aim around 520 jin? No, I will say it plainly: about 520 kilograms per mu.

For maize, I will save some labor and money by going with hard-stubble sowing after wheat, so mostly no-tillage. Summer rain usually helps maize, so I will irrigate less than wheat, but if the stand comes up uneven or it turns dry around big bell stage, I will give it water. I will use hybrid maize seed because around here that is what gives the better ear. I will still feed it enough nitrogen, because maize likes to eat, but I will not throw fertilizer blindly. I will spray about two times, mainly for weeds early and then insects or leaf disease if they come. If weather is decent, I will look for about 580 kilograms per mu.
